I'm aware that a partial copy is available from the Department's website with redactions for commercially sensitive information. I'm seeking a full unredacted copy because, in accordance with the Freedom of Information act, public interest overrides the commercially sensitive nature of any information in the contract for the following reasons: - Then Minister Richard Bruton, who signed the contract, told the Joint Committee on Communications, Climate Action and Environment on May 14, 2019: "The contract will be published in full when it is finalised." This promise to the Oireachtas in itself constitutes a matter of overriding public interest. - Accounts filed by National Broadband Ireland companies show they have been insufficiently capitalised to date and the release of the full contract including detailed financial requirements is necessary to allow scrutiny of the project and protect up to €2.97 billion in associated state subsidies. - National Broadband Ireland ceased operating in a competitive market when it became the sole bidder for the National Broadband Plan and this position was confirmed by the signature of the contract. As it has no competitors, the commercial sensitiveness of any information pertaining to it is irrelevant. 2. All documents exchanged between the National Development Finance Agency (NDFA) and the Department as part of the pre-qualification process of the bidder now known as National Broadband Ireland under the procurement process for the National Broadband Plan prior to its appointment as preferred bidder, between January 1, 2019 and May 10, 2019. 3. I therefore request that, where necessary, new record(s) be created, under Section 17(4) of the FOI Act 2014, for the purpose of collating the requested details — particularly in relation to total pay received, biographical information, and the full timeline of appointments and resignations. I would note that, in relation to remuneration, I am looking for both the pay rate and the actual remuneration paid during their tenure. Whilst it may be argued that the actual remuneration is personal information I would note that the OIC has taken the view that "persons in receipt of remuneration sourced from public funds should have a diminished expectation of privacy or confidentiality in relation to that remuneration." Particularly, case 090149 specifically found against the idea that an applicant, the CEO of a public service body, "could have had a reasonable expectation that his level of remuneration would never be disclosed to the public. The Commissioner also considered that release of the salary details at issue would not be a hugely significant invasion of the rights to privacy of the applicant to the extent that disclosure of health or other personal details might be."

name: Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment
request_description: 1. All correspondence — including emails, letters, memoranda, minutes of meetings, and any other written communications — between the Department (including any of its divisions or officials acting in their official capacity) and the European Commission (or any of its services, including DG Energy) concerning the implementation of Article 12 of the Energy Efficiency Directive (EU) 2023/1791 and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364, in particular regarding data centre reporting obligations, the confidentiality of reported data, and the public disclosure of data centre energy performance information. Time period: 1 January 2023 to present. 2. All data centre energy performance reports submitted to the Department or through the Department to the European database pursuant to Article 12 EED, or any summaries, compilations, or analyses of such reports held by the Department. 3. Any internal guidance, policy documents, or legal assessments produced by or for the Department regarding the interpretation of the trade secrets and confidentiality exemptions under Article 12(1) EED and Article 5 of the Delegated Regulation, as applied to data centre reporting in Ireland. 4. Any correspondence between the Department and the Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI) or the Commission for Regulation of Utilities (CRU) regarding the implementation of Article 12 EED and the handling of data centre energy performance data. Request amended on 02/04/2026 Please take the scope of this part of the request to cover correspondence with the European Commission in relation to the implementation of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364, in particular regarding data centre reporting obligations, the confidentiality of reported data, and the public disclosure of data centre energy performance information, for the period from 6 June 2024 to the present. Regarding point 2, I note your clarification that data centre operators report directly into the European database and that no reports are held by the Department in that form. However, as you note yourself, Member States have access pursuant to Article 5(3) of the Delegated Regulation to all information communicated to the European database by data centres in their territory. On that basis, I would like to amend this part of my request as follows: I request that the Department retrieve and provide to me the data reported to the European database by individual data centres located in Ireland, as accessible to the Department under Article 5(3). I would note that Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 is a delegated act adopted under Article 290 TFEU. Article 5(5) of that Regulation cannot override the rights of access to environmental information established under Directive 2003/4/EC, as transposed into Irish law by the European Communities (Access to Information on the Environment) Regulations 2007–2018. A blanket policy of confidentiality applied to all data points, without individual assessment, is not consistent with these obligations. Should the Department consider that specific data points are exempt from disclosure, I would ask that a justification be provided in each individual case, specifying which exemption applies and why. Regarding point 3, I am glad this can be searched for and look forward to the results. Regarding point 4, I am happy to withdraw this part of the request.

request_description: I request access to the following categories of records: 1. Initial Development and Implementation of the DRS • Copies of any feasibility studies, impact assessments, or consultation documents related to the Deposit Return Scheme, including reports discussing the expected environmental benefits, economic impact, and public feedback prior to its introduction. • Records, meeting minutes, presentations, and correspondence relating to the proposal, design, and implementation phases of the DRS. • All correspondence between the Department of the Environment, Climate and Communications and the Department of Finance or any other relevant governmental department about the budget and projected costs of the DRS, particularly discussions on the financing of the reverse vending machines and operational logistics. • Records detailing the selection of the paper type used for the issuance of DRS vouchers and any subsequent reviews or internal discussions on the sustainability of these materials. 2. Meetings and Consultations • Minutes of all meetings, consultations, and working groups held between government officials, private companies (including Re-turn and any other companies involved in the scheme), environmental advocacy groups, and other stakeholders regarding the establishment and execution of the DRS. • Details of any public or private consultations carried out to determine the format, scale, and operation of the DRS, including feedback from stakeholders. 3. Environmental and Economic Impact Reports • Any environmental impact assessments or reviews that were carried out since the launch of the DRS, specifically in relation to its carbon footprint, transport logistics, and the impact of using non-recyclable materials for vouchers. • Correspondence and documents related to any environmental concerns or criticisms raised internally or by third parties about the operational efficiency or environmental efficacy of the DRS. 4. Contractual Agreements and Funding • Copies of all contracts and agreements entered into between the Irish Government and third parties involved in the DRS, including Re-turn, vending machine suppliers, and logistics providers. • Records relating to the funding sources and cost breakdown of the scheme, including the distribution of expenses for machine installation, maintenance, voucher issuance, and advertising campaigns. 5. Monitoring, Compliance, and Reviews • Any documents outlining the monitoring, compliance, and evaluation mechanisms for the DRS, including performance reviews, regular audits, or reports assessing whether the scheme has met its stated goals. • Records of any internal reviews or discussions about modifying or adjusting the scheme in response to public feedback or operational challenges. 6. Communications with Elected Representatives • All correspondence between the Department and any elected representatives discussing the DRS, including any concerns raised about its environmental impact, the choice of materials for vouchers, and compliance with existing waste reduction laws. • Copies of any briefing notes, memos, or advisories provided to Ministers or the Taoiseach’s office in relation to the DRS. 7. Advertising and Public Communication • Copies of all advertising, public communication strategies, and educational materials designed to inform the public about the DRS, including details on messaging around sustainability and environmental impact. • All records of discussions on how to address public concerns regarding the non- recyclable nature of the DRS vouchers and any proposed changes to mitigate these issues. 8. Records Relating to the Voucher System • Full technical specifications and sustainability assessments for the materials used in the production of DRS vouchers. • Documentation and correspondence related to any decisions made about voucher design, selection of materials, and alternative options considered for making the vouchers recyclable. • Internal discussions and correspondence following public or media reports that highlighted the environmental concerns of using non-recyclable materials.

name: Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment
request_description: I request access to environmental information held by the Department of the Environment, Climate and Communications under the European Communities (Access to Information on the Environment) Regulations 2007–2018 concerning the preparation, methodology, data sourcing, validation, and publication of the National Territory Map for Grid-Scale Solar PV ("the National Map"), published on 3 September 2025 under Article 15b of Directive (EU) 2023/2413 (Renewable Energy Directive III, “RED III”). The information sought concerns measures affecting land use, landscape, biodiversity, soil, and spatial planning across the national territory. It falls within Article 3(1)(a), (b), (c), (d), and (e) of the AIE Regulations. Timeframe 1 January 2022 to the date of this request. ………………………………………………. On 02/04/2026 the request was refined to Information Sought Records documenting the Department's validation, quality assurance, and verification procedures applied to local authority LARES solar data before incorporation into the national Territory Map, including: 1. Any record or records identifying which local authorities submitted or provided LARES solar mapping data, the date of receipt, and the format in which data was provided (GIS shapefiles, raster datasets, tabular, development plan excerpts, or other). 2. Documentation of quality assurance or validation procedures applied to local authority LARES solar data, including any testing for methodological consistency, spatial coverage gaps, attribute completeness, or alignment with national suitability criteria. 3. National-level reconciliation or harmonisation records addressing how methodological discrepancies between local authority LARES datasets were identified and resolved before publication in the national Map. 4. Technical specifications or guidance documents issued by the Department to local authorities specifying the required methodology, data standards, or suitability tier definitions to be applied in LARES preparation. (Search period for this item: 1 January 2018 - 31 December 2021.) 5. Internal decision documents or briefing memoranda addressing whether local authority LARES data met the Department's quality assurance requirements before publication in the national Territory Map. Scope Clarification & Exclusions The following scope limitations apply:  Document type: Quality assurance reports, validation assessments, internal decision memoranda, data intake logs, and technical guidance only. Excluded: draft iterations and general email correspondence. Formal correspondence containing methodological determinations, validation results, or quality assurance findings is not excluded.  Scope: National-level validation and quality assurance procedures only. Not requested: individual project assessments, site-specific reviews, or records relating to specific projects approved under the national Map.  Timeframe: 1 January 2021 - 3 September 2025 (from final LARES adoption through national Map publication), save that item 4 above carries a search period of 1 January 2018 – 31 December 2021.  Format: Electronic access, original format. Contractor-Held Records Where any of the above records are held by contractors acting on behalf of the Department, including Compass Informatics, I request that the Department take all reasonable steps to retrieve those records in accordance with Article 3(1) of the AIE Regulations.

request_description: Scope / time period Please search records from 1 January 2003 to present, or the earliest date for which relevant records are held. This period includes Ireland’s preparation for, and implementation of, the EU Energy Performance of Buildings Directive and subsequent policy evolution. Environmental information requested (non-exhaustive) 1. Any policy papers, briefing notes, submissions to Ministers, impact assessments, or internal guidance held by the Department that discuss: • the scope and objectives of BER or related energy-performance policy, and • whether indoor environmental quality, radon risk, ventilation, moisture/mould, or health impacts were considered. 2. Any correspondence (including emails, letters, or meeting records) between the Department and SEAI, DHLGH, EPA, HSE, NSAI, or EU institutions referencing: • radon or radon risk, • ventilation or airtightness, • indoor air quality, moisture or mould, • or health and wellbeing impacts associated with energy-efficiency or retrofit policy. 3. Any records of interdepartmental groups, committees, consultations, or stakeholder engagements where potential interactions between energy efficiency objectives and human health or indoor environmental quality were discussed. 4. Any documents addressing whether Ireland’s national environmental or public-health context, including its elevated radon risk profile, warranted specific consideration or policy treatment when transposing or implementing EU energy-performance requirements. 5. Any records reflecting consideration of potential trade-offs between climate/energy objectives and indoor environmental quality or health, including whether safeguards or complementary measures were discussed. 6. Any records, memoranda, briefing notes, or correspondence indicating that radon, indoor air quality, ventilation-related health impacts, or moisture/mould were considered to fall outside the scope of energy-performance or BER policy, including any rationale recorded for such exclusion or deferral to other regulatory frameworks. Subject focus • Records relating to: • the BER Advisory Report and its revision to include information on radon; • consideration of radon risk within energy performance / BER policy; • any assessment of the interaction between energy efficiency measures, airtightness, ventilation, and radon exposure. Clarification of scope (to avoid ambiguity) For clarity, the request is focused on policy development and consideration, including: • briefing notes, policy papers, submissions, and decision records relating to: • why radon information was incorporated into the BER Advisory Report; • the extent to which radon risk was treated as advisory versus risk-mitigating; • whether ventilation trade-offs associated with energy efficiency measures were considered in that context. I am not seeking: • routine administrative correspondence, • individual dwelling files, • or records duplicated in other departments’ holdings.

Geophysical and Magnetic Anomaly Records Materials to be searched: • Magnetic anomaly maps • Gravity survey records • Electromagnetic disturbance reports Suggested search terms: • “localized magnetic spike” • “EM field disruption” • “magnetic signature – no geological match” • “compass deviation” • “short-duration high-field anomaly” 3. Irish National Seismic Network (ISNN) Data Materials to be searched: • Seismic event logs and waveforms • Bulletins referencing non-tectonic events • Internal memos explaining seismic data with no geophysical source Suggested search terms: • “airburst-like seismic event” • “non-seismic waveform” • “high-altitude source” • “pressure signal unexplained” • “sonic boom with no aircraft confirmed” 4. Duty Geologist Logs and Public Queries Materials to be searched: • Email logs at duty.geologist@gsi.ie • Public query summaries • Field reports following site visits Suggested search terms: • “burned soil” or “scorched vegetation” • “circular ground impression” • “trace evidence of aerial object” • “soil radiation spike” • “unusual plant growth” • “metal fragment reported by public” 5. Geochemical and Physical Sample Analysis Records Materials to be searched: • Lab test reports (mineralogical, spectrographic, elemental) • Unclassified sample investigations • Communications with other agencies regarding unidentified material Suggested search terms: • “sample origin unknown” • “non-standard alloy” • “metallic fragment – not natural” • “high-purity magnesium” • “fused metal / slag – unidentified source” • “microsphere analysis” 6. Internal and Interagency Correspondence Materials to be searched: • Email archives of staff in marine, geophysics, and minerals sections • Memos and meeting notes involving anomaly reporting • Correspondence with other state bodies (e.g. Defence Forces, Marine Institute, Met Éireann) Suggested search terms: • “UAP” • “UFO” • “unidentified aerial” • “radar contact unexplained” • “Defence Forces query – aerial object” • “interagency meeting – UAP”
